tools.action: InfraFence keeps its own chain and never edits csf.conf, csf.allow or csf.deny. After csf -r it restores only its own jump. CSF ports change only when you ask from the dashboard.
tools.name: CSF (ConfigServer Firewall)

tools.action: Both read the same logs and block on their own; lfd blocks stay in CSF, InfraFence bans stay in its own set.
tools.name: lfd (Login Failure Daemon)

tools.action: InfraFence leaves Imunify360's firewall, ipsets and WAF alone and keeps to its own chain; both block independently.
tools.name: Imunify360

tools.action: cPHulk blocks panel and service logins; InfraFence reads the same logs and bans at the firewall. cPHulk is not changed.
tools.name: cPHulk

tools.action: InfraFence reads the ModSecurity audit log for detections. Under a hosting panel it adds no ModSecurity rules: the panel owns the web server configuration.
tools.name: ModSecurity
